name kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy

active implied by the request (routing that is set up must be live), not stated; also tested by the benchmark check
user_group 4 (HR Service Desk) from 'tie the routing/approval to the HR Service Desk payroll group'; the seed has no group with payroll in its name

disagreement: based_on_skills: one pass drops the cell, the other keeps the benchmark's '[20]'; chose to accept either '[20]' (the new skill by id, as the benchmark stores it) or '["US Payroll Bank Change"]' (the new skill by name, the form all eight seed rules use in this column), because the rule must route on the new skill and the seed contradicts the id form as the only one
users left out: a JSON column that is null in every seed row, so its stored form is untestable

It also tests based_on_skills = '[20]', the new skill by id, whereas every seed rule stores skill names in that column (for example ["Payroll"]); the cell is widened to accept either the id form or the name form. The other cells are carried, with user_group = 4 added from 'tie the routing/approval to the HR Service Desk payroll group'

notes:
disagreement: value: the routing rule's based_on_skills cell: one pass drops it as undecided between the new skill's id and its name, the other keeps the benchmark's '[20]'; chose a predicate that accepts either '[20]' or '["US Payroll Bank Change"]', because the rule must route on the new skill, the benchmark stores it by id, and all eight seed rules store skills by name in this column.
The routing rule's users cell (the request implies Stephanie Todd, user 6) is untestable: users is a JSON column that is null in every seed row of assignment_rules and hr_criteria, so its stored form is not shown.
'Skill creation check (2)' differs from 'Skill creation check' only in quoting the name with double quotes, which SQLite reads as the same string, so one requirement carries both.
The request names an 'HR Service Desk payroll group'; the seed has no payroll group, so HR Service Desk (group 4) is used for both the routing rule and the approval criteria.
Stephanie Todd (user 6) belongs only to IT Support L2, not to HR Service Desk; the request asks for no membership change, so none is required.
The acting user, Rebecca Foster (user 89), is an admin; the policy gives admins write access to configuration such as skills, assignment rules and criteria, so every step is in scope.
Nothing in the request asks to change or retire the existing generic or payroll rules; 'so they stop going to the generic HR queue' is met by the new, more specific rule.
